title: Energy for strict complex oblique boundary conditions
completed_component_scope: Smooth strict complex oblique weighted energy, variable coefficients and lower terms, compact slabs, exact strictness tests.
reviewed_arguments: Exact source F,E determinant and D=-i∂ conversion include the datum and temporal-positive Lorentz convention.
Adding iN∧W changes no principal operator; the actual density and skew derivatives remain in the first coefficients.
The complete differentiated current retains every complex lower, density, multiplier and mass term and cancels the Hessian pairs exactly.
Electric bivectors contribute zero to the current. The actual projected spatial block has e_Z=fe/sqrt(f²-κ²), with a uniform strict margin.
Real future conormals satisfy the positive Hermitian Cauchy-Schwarz bound on the original physical cone, including null artificial faces.
The outward natural derivative is N-iW. The full complex 2×2 boundary matrix, its determinant and all remaining directions give coercivity.
Arbitrary principal boundary residuals are split off in the normal component; boundary zeroth terms are absorbed by a fixed positive mass.
A finite defining-function construction and the exact smooth flow give a common collar. The skew tensor is cut off before the future multiplier is blended.
A single global current avoids partition-of-solution commutators. Empty-boundary and zero tangential spatial dimension cases are treated directly.
Actual divergence and coarea signs, zero initial flux, sequential mass and weight choices prove the full stated weighted inequality.
The neutral cutoff family disproves the no-loss extension at δ=0. The growing cutoff family disproves every stated finite-integer-derivative residual estimate for e>1.
Three complete solutions retain source signs, a large imaginary temporal coefficient, exact rational bounds, mode roots and all product-rule residuals.
The entire new desktop reader, original figure and two mobile samples were actually inspected. Every formula and figure horizontal extent was measured accessible.
